correctness.rationale: The \(m+2\)-state chain is finite and irreducible. Its resource indicator has stationary balance \((c+e)p_m+kq_m=c\). A cycle from the resource-absent state has mean absent time \(1/c\) and occupied mean \(L_m=\int_0^\infty e^{-et}s(t)^m\,dt\) with independent killed on/off specialists. Hence \(p_m=cL_m/(1+cL_m)\) and \(q_m=c(1-eL_m)/[k(1+cL_m)]\). Positive \(u,k\) imply \(0<s(t)<1\) for every \(t>0\), so \(L_m\) strictly decreases and \(q_m\) strictly increases. The Feynman–Kac Taylor expansion \(\log s(t)=-uk t^2/2+O(t^3)\), dominated Laplace scaling, and the exact richness formula yield the \(c/k\) limit and leading \(m^{-1/2}\) constant. Reproducible exact-rational stationary and renewal resolvent computations agree on 66 cases; these checks do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The fully accessible 2010 ecological occupancy article defines resource-triggered secondary losses and biodiversity-inhibiting consumers, but uses a ten-species simulation to classify impacts and does not derive the all-guild exact threshold, strict size monotonicity, or many-consumer scaling. The 1982 population-dependent catastrophe work is substantially relevant background, but its accessible abstract concerns broader discrete population losses and does not settle the specific guild-richness ordering; its inaccessible full text is a stated priority risk. Independent stationary-balance and regenerative-process methods are prior mathematics; originality is asserted only for the combined concrete theorem within inspected evidence.
residual_risks: Historical population-dependent-catastrophe full texts (especially Brockwell–Gani–Resnick 1982) remained inaccessible, so priority remains provisional.
Generic Markov-resolvent literature may encode related calculations in alternate queueing notation; no claim of independently verified historical uniqueness is made.
The ecological universality holds only under exact symmetric resource-dependent extinction and independent consumer arrival assumptions.

value.rationale: The exact phase boundary answers the source’s substantive classification problem—when a trophic consumer guild raises or reduces stationary realized species richness—even though more potential consumers always increase their own total occupancy. The dependence on potential guild size can be strictly negative at every increment, has a universal neutral line \(\(k=c+e\)\), and approaches a finite parameter-independent richness ceiling \(\(c/k\)\) with quantified rate. This is a structural ecological benchmark for the simplest resource-mediated extirpation module; it is more than a single numerical example, while no empirical relevance outside the model is claimed.
